defects.description: The upload-URL request goes directly from the browser to Lambda, bypassing the defined API Gateway authorizer, but no Function URL or authenticated Lambda invocation mechanism is specified; route this request through the protected API.
Object-created notifications and thumbnail output use the same bucket without a specified input-prefix filter or output exclusion, creating a recursive-invocation risk when thumbnails are saved.
Bucket access policies, CloudFront origin access control, least-privilege Lambda roles, and author-specific upload authorization are unspecified; encryption alone does not establish these controls.

The thumbnail DLQ and CloudWatch services are listed without an explicit failure-destination association, retry policy, actionable alarms, or recovery procedure; welcome-email retries and idempotency are also unspecified.
Cache behaviors, TTLs, invalidation, and authorization-header handling are unspecified; distinguish cacheable published reads from authenticated or subscriber-specific operations.
The expected-load clarification remains a question rather than a chosen assumption, and DynamoDB capacity mode and any paid API Gateway cache allocation are not addressed.

reviews.summary: The serverless service selection fits the blog, but the upload-URL path, same-bucket thumbnail processing, and incomplete security and failure-handling details need correction.

defects.description: Cognito is included, but the API Gateway configuration does not attach a user-pool authorizer or identify protected methods, leaving enforcement of authentication for author and upload operations unspecified.
Object-created notifications and thumbnail output use the same bucket without a specified input-prefix filter or output exclusion, creating a recursive-invocation risk when thumbnails are saved.
Bucket access policies, CloudFront origin access control, least-privilege Lambda roles, and author-specific restrictions on presigned uploads are unspecified.

Failure-destination handling is stated as an intention, but its DLQ association, retry policy, alarms, and recovery procedure are not detailed; welcome-email retries and idempotency are also unspecified.
Cache behaviors, TTLs, invalidation, and authorization-header handling are unspecified; distinguish cacheable published reads from authenticated or subscriber-specific operations.
The expected-load clarification remains a question rather than a chosen assumption, and DynamoDB capacity mode and any paid API Gateway cache allocation are not addressed.

reviews.summary: The design provides an appropriate serverless blog foundation and correctly routes upload-URL requests through API Gateway, but authorization and thumbnail-loop prevention remain unresolved.

defects.description: The HTTP API is shown forwarding directly to private Fargate tasks without a supported private integration target or VPC link; provide an ALB/NLB listener or Cloud Map service and the required VPC link.
Both availability zones depend on the single NAT gateway in AZ 1, so loss of that AZ removes payments connectivity even if application tasks remain available elsewhere.
The session cache has no cross-AZ replica, Multi-AZ setting, or automatic failover configuration, so it does not establish the required availability-zone resilience.

Automatic credential rotation is asserted without selecting an RDS-managed rotation mechanism or configuring a Secrets Manager rotation workflow and schedule; application retrieval and adoption of rotated credentials are also absent.

The HTTP API's Cognito authentication intent is not translated into its supported JWT authorizer configuration, including a Cognito issuer and audience; a REST API user-pool authorizer configuration is not interchangeable with an HTTP API JWT authorizer.
The multi-AZ task deployment is stated in prose but not made concrete through an ECS service, both subnet IDs, and a minimum task count sufficient to retain capacity after an AZ failure.
Security-group restrictions, task IAM roles, database/cache TLS, scaling assumptions, log delivery, and actionable alarms remain unspecified.

reviews.summary: Fargate and managed PostgreSQL are appropriate choices, but the ingress path is incomplete and the single NAT gateway and unreplicated cache fail the required AZ-loss resilience.

reviews.summary: The explicit Cognito authentication flow improves clarity, but the design retains a non-working ingress integration and major gaps in AZ resilience and credential rotation.

defects.description: At-rest encryption is not specified for either Aurora or the session cache; explicitly enable encryption for both rather than treating private subnet placement as protection for stored data.

Client credentials produces access tokens, but no required OAuth scopes are specified on REST API methods; a Cognito authorizer without method scopes treats the supplied token as an identity token, so configure resource-server scopes and enforce them on protected methods.
Show clients obtaining tokens from Cognito separately from API Gateway validating JWTs; the API Gateway-to-Cognito OAuth invocation edge is not an accurate depiction of the token-validation protocol.
Specify security-group relationships, least-privilege task and proxy roles, TLS for database/cache connections, task authentication to RDS Proxy, and the selected automatic-rotation mechanism.

Make the intended HA deployment concrete with both subnet attachments, minimum task capacity, Aurora reader placement, and cache replica/failover settings; also define failover retries, payment idempotency, alarms, and restore testing.

For the assumed modest workload, quantify Aurora instance capacity and the incremental benefit of RDS Proxy so the additional managed-service baseline is justified; the two NAT gateways are justified by the HA requirement.

reviews.summary: The architecture addresses the requested multi-AZ topology and private container operation, but encryption and access-token authorization need explicit configuration before deployment.

reviews.summary: The design covers the requested managed, private, multi-AZ architecture and explicitly encrypts stateful services, with remaining work concentrated in authorization and deployment-level security and recovery settings.

preference.why: B routes upload-URL requests through the existing API Gateway rather than an undefined direct Lambda endpoint, although its authorizer must be explicitly attached and both designs need thumbnail-loop protection.
B marginally improves authentication clarity by including the Cognito pool and client sign-in path, but neither design is deployable as drawn or satisfies end-to-end AZ-loss resilience.
Both address the enabled Multi-AZ priority, but B additionally specifies encryption for Aurora and ElastiCache and makes the ALB's cross-AZ intent clearer.
